release_claim.reason: Both R3 operational findings pass focused tests and affected governed gates, but a new exact audit artifact, independent verification, and deferred full certification remain outstanding.

findings.finding: Host and Python canonicalize valid JSON payloads differently
findings.root_cause: The host hashed JavaScript JSON formatting while Python recomputed a hash after parsing with different number formatting and key-order semantics.
findings.repair: The host now signs the SHA-256 of the exact UTF-8 payload JSON and carries that representation in the proof. Python verifies those exact bytes, parses the signed payload as the authoritative operation input, and rejects a separately supplied mismatch without cross-runtime reserialization.

findings.finding: Workflow post-cancel campaign can fail and retain active resource records
findings.root_cause: Terminal cancellation could become externally visible before the durable session worker closed its resource record; resource updates also used a non-atomic get/upsert pair and repeated completion was not idempotent. Node failure receipts dropped the exception message and correlation context.
findings.repair: Durable workflow cancellation now finalizes the session resource before publishing the terminal state, current-process completion is idempotent, resource updates are one locked transaction, and every node attempt retains a bounded sanitized failure message plus deterministic correlation ID.

non_blocking_debt.summary: R3 independently confirmed 157 same-file duplicate selectors, 193 duplicate occurrences, zero cross-file duplicates, and passing contrast checks.
